text:
nightly-bot: [ALERT] Nightly eval failure for rwd-7b-v2 INT8 (calibrated). Metric drop: -4.7% accuracy on commonsense_qa_promptset vs fp16 baseline. Report: https://internal.reports/ci/1710643200 (includes diffs + sample gens).

maria: saw the alert, thanks. any sample bad gens in the report?

nightly-bot: included 12 failing examples, top failures show hallucinations and truncated completions for prompts that were OK in fp16. Attached: /artifacts/1710643200/fail_examples.json

sam: quick look — reproduces locally when I run the quantized build. Command I ran:
```
./scripts/run_eval.sh --model rwd-7b-v2 --quant int8 --calib-set nightly_calib_v3 --promptset commonsense_qa --seed 42 --batch 8
```
Outputs the same low accuracy.

kai: can you paste one or two failed prompts+outs inline? easier to eyeball.

sam: copying two examples:
1) prompt: "Why did the cat hide under the couch?"
   fp16: "Because it was scared of the thunder and wanted a safe space."
   int8: "Because the couch is made of wood and eats cats."
2) prompt: "How can you reduce salt in a recipe?"
   fp16: "Use low-sodium broth or reduce added salt; taste and adjust."
   int8: "Add sugar then bake at 500F."

maria: those are clear semantic regressions, not just tokenization shifts. Did the quant pipeline change recently? calibration dataset changed?

jonah: we updated calib set two nights ago to calib_v3 (smaller, more diverse) to speed up pipeline. also toggled per-layer folding for faster inference.

kai: suspect 2 possibilities: (1) calibration dataset distribution shift causing poor scale estimates for activation outliers, (2) folding/graph transform introduced numerical patterns that quantize badly. we should check layer-wise min/max and histograms.

eva: throwing in three more failures from the report (short):
- prompt: "What does a lighthouse do?" -> int8: "It is a small lamp used for baking"
- prompt: "Best way to clean a dishwasher" -> int8: "Use lemon oil on circuit board"
- prompt: "What's the capital of France?" -> int8: "Berlin"

maria: ok. @sam can you dump per-layer range stats for fp16 vs int8 calib run? e.g. max_abs per layer, and compare calib_v2 vs calib_v3. Kai, any quick script?

kai: yes, use the quant-stats tool:
```
python tools/quant_stats.py --model checkpoints/rwd-7b-v2 --calib calib_v3 --out /tmp/stats_v3.json
python tools/quant_stats.py --model checkpoints/rwd-7b-v2 --calib calib_v2 --out /tmp/stats_v2.json
```
Look for layers with >10x change in max_abs or many NaNs.

sam: ran it. top hit: attention.mlp.fc2 (layer 23) max_abs_v2=3.1, max_abs_v3=72.9. lots of outliers in calib_v3. I think calib_v3 picks up a few extremely long-tail activations that blow up scale.

maria: that explains catastrophic clipping — int8 scale gets huge and saturates other activations. Did we use symmetric per-tensor quant or per-channel?

jonah: pipeline default is symmetric per-tensor for weights, per-channel for weights was disabled to simplify runtime. activations are per-tensor symmetric.

kai: two remediation ideas: (A) switch activations to per-channel (if supported) or (B) keep per-tensor but apply outlier clipping / histogram-based percentile (e.g., 99.9%) during calibration. Also try revert to calib_v2 quickly to confirm cause.

sam: quick AB test: re-ran calibration with calib_v2 and 99.9% clipping. accuracy recovered to -0.6% vs fp16 (within noise). so calib_v3 + no-clipping is the root cause.

maria: great find. so options: revert calib_v3, or change calibration algorithm (percentile clipping) or enable per-channel for problematic layers. Performance tradeoffs?

jonah: enabling per-channel increases memory bandwidth and slightly slows runtime but should be limited to weights only. activation per-channel is harder on current runtime. Percentile clipping is cheap.

eva: any risk that calib_v3 was added to cover real distribution shift — if we revert we might lose long-tail behavior coverage.

kai: we can hybridize: keep calib_v3 but apply 99.9% clipping and log outlier examples for manual review. Also add a diagnostic that flags layers with >20x change in max_abs between calib versions.

maria: agreed. action items:
- sam: implement 99.9% clipping in quant calib and re-run nightly (low effort) — due today.
- kai: add diff-stat diagnostic and alert when max_abs ratio > 20x — due tomorrow.
- jonah: rollback the pipeline change that disabled per-channel weight quant (or at least enable for layers flagged) — sync with infra/serving if this impacts runtime images.
- eva: curate a set of outlier prompts from calib_v3 and add to our eval promptset to prevent silent regressions.

sam: on it, kicking off a job now. Command I'm using:
```
./scripts/run_calib.sh --model rwd-7b-v2 --calib calib_v3 --clip-pct 99.9 --out /tmp/calib_v3_clipped
./scripts/run_eval.sh --model rwd-7b-v2 --quant int8 --calib /tmp/calib_v3_clipped --promptset commonsense_qa
```
Will post results in ~20m.

nightly-bot: note: scheduling heuristic will re-run nightly with updated artifacts if new calib artifacts are uploaded to /artifacts.

maria: perfect. let's keep the root thread here. if sam's job recovers accuracy, we can push a hotfix to the pipeline and mark this resolved. if not, escalate to deeper numeric debugging (FP8 simulation, per-layer quant sensitivity tests).

sam: first quick result: with 99.9% clipping on calib_v3 accuracy delta is -0.9% vs fp16. still a small gap but acceptable for now. I'm uploading the new artifact.

maria: thanks. please create a short postmortem note in #eng-ml with the regression summary, root cause (calib_v3 outliers + no clipping), and the fix (percentile clipping + diag). also add a JIRA: INF-3421.

jonah: I'll schedule a follow-up next week to decide if we keep calib_v3 or expand calib set differently.

kai: other long-term items: test FP8 emulation to see whether narrower dynamic range helps or hurts, and run per-layer sensitivity sweeps (quant granularity, clipping pct).

maria: thanks team. closing here once the pipeline hotfix lands. :thumbsup:
